analysis.sign_in_again: You have to sign in again
analysis.title: Analysis
app.no_accounts_body: Import your configuration (accounts, categories and rules) and Money will interpret the movements your banks bring.
app.sign_in_again: You have to sign in again
backup.hint: Accounts, categories, rules, labels, declared income and the history, in one file. Importing replaces what there is.
backup.not_config: That file is not a Money configuration.
backup.replace_consequence: The current accounts, categories, rules, labels, recorded expenses and income are replaced by the file's. Download a backup first if you want to be able to go back.
backup.title: Configuration backup
category.basic_hint: Turn it off for what you could do without (Leisure, Travel): it leaves basic spending.
category.label: {name} · {ownership} {nature}
category.living_hint: Turn it off for what is not living (Work): it leaves monthly spending.
category.name: Name
category.renamed: It is also renamed in the history.
composition.name_hint: The name as your institution shows it: it is recognised even if “Hedged” or “Fund” changes. Cash is “Cash”.
composition.table: Each fund, the products it is in and how much it weighs
composition.unknown: {amount} with no breakdown: products whose funds are unknown, or unclassified funds. They are recorded in Settings › Accounts and products.
composition.what_asset: How much of the portfolio is equity, bonds, real estate, cash or crypto
composition.what_fund: How much of the portfolio each fund is, adding up the same fund across products
composition.what_product: How much of the portfolio each product is
composition.what_region: Where the portfolio is invested, by region
emergency.detail: It changes the fund's target and which account counts as cash.
emergency.hint: The fund's target is your monthly basic spending times these months. That account does not count as cash.
emergency.title: Emergency fund
entry.by_me: Yours in cash with no withdrawal that explains it. If it came from a cash machine, label the withdrawal instead.
entry.by_other: Counts as paid by {other}: their part goes up and yours too, according to the category.
entry.title: Expense outside any account
filter.title: Filters
flow.cycle_hint: Each cycle goes from the day the pay cheque comes in ({day}) to the day before the next, and belongs to the month it pays: one that comes in from the 25th, to the next month.
flow.history_hint: Before the cut-off the history only has monthly sums, so those stretches are calendar months, with the end-of-month pay cheque in the next. The first stretch after the cut-off carries the pay cheque of the history's last month{moved}.
flow.info_income: What comes in during the period: the pay cheque and other income. With “All”, also what the other person puts into the shared, so the shared shows whole.
flow.info_invested: What was contributed to your investment products minus what was taken out. What was paid to your home as rent counts as shared spending, not here.
flow.info_invested_rent: What was contributed to your investment products minus what was taken out. What was paid to your home as split rent counts here, not as spending.
flow.info_left: What comes in minus what you spend and invest: what stays in your accounts. If negative, that period you drew on savings. The savings rate is what was invested plus what is left, over what comes in.
flow.info_spent: Your individual spending and, of the shared, your part (or all of it, if you choose).
flow.nothing: Nothing to show in this period.
flow.open: The last stretch has not ended: it is missing what arrives until the next pay cheque.
flow.rate_detail: What was invested plus what is left, over what comes in
flow.sankey: The period's money, from income to each destination
flow.title: Flow
flow.unlogged_one: One month of the history has no individual spending recorded: what was left in it, minus what was missing, counts as “Unlabelled” individual spending. It does not draw on your savings: if more is missing than is left, the difference comes in as “Unlabelled”.
flow.unlogged_other: {count} months of the history have no individual spending recorded: what was left in them, minus what was missing, counts as “Unlabelled” individual spending. They do not draw on your savings: if more is missing than is left, the difference comes in as “Unlabelled”.
flow.where: Where it comes from and where it goes
fund.hint: What you say applies to this fund in all your products.
fund.reset: Go back to what the catalogue says
fund.sum_wrong: They add up to {percent}: they have to add up to 100%, or nothing if you do not want to split it.
fund.unclassified_body: It is not in the catalogue: tell me what it is to split it in the composition.
health.less: The bank's balance has {amount} less than its movements: a charge has yet to arrive. If it is recent, it fixes itself when the bank publishes it.
health.more: The bank's balance has {amount} more than its movements: an income has yet to arrive. If it is recent, it fixes itself when the bank publishes it.
incomes.detail: They change the split of the proportional for the whole year, and with it the balance.
incomes.hint: The yearly salary is prorated by the days of the range, and the extra is spread across them.
incomes.space_hint: The space where you both see the shared money.
incomes.title: Income of {year}
invest.by_month_chart: What was contributed to each product, month by month
invest.carried: · Worth their last valuation plus what was contributed after; their gain of these days is not known yet.
invest.chart: Value and contributed capital of {what} at the end of each month
invest.estimated: · Estimated on {day} with their funds' prices since their last snapshot; they are corrected when another is uploaded.
invest.info_gain: What they are worth minus what you contributed (put in minus taken out) since the beginning. The simple return is that gain over what was contributed, regardless of when you put it in.
invest.info_period: What was earned in the period: what they are worth at the end minus what they were worth at the start and minus what was contributed in between. The percentage weighs each contribution by the days it was in (modified Dietz), and is not annualised.
invest.info_value: What your investment products are worth on the last day of the period (or today). A shared product counts by your share, unless you choose “All”.
invest.info_xirr: The IRR: the yearly return an account would have needed to end with the same, putting in each contribution on the day you did. It is the one to compare with a deposit or with inflation. Before the cut-off, the history's contributions go in the middle of their month.
invest.none: No investment products with contributions or value yet.
invest.other: {name}: besides yours, {other} has contributed {amount}. The value you see is your share.
invest.title: Investment
invest.widened: The 12 months up to the end of the period.
invest.with_dates: With the date of each contribution
movements.in_out: What comes in: what goes out and what is left
movements.over: · {amount} more goes out than comes in
movements.sum: What the movements you see add up to
movements.title: Movements
movements.to_label_hint: Cash and what no rule explains. Until you label it, it does not count as spending.
movements.try_less: Try fewer filters or another period.
new.hint: Without an account of your sources, its movements come from the transfers from your other accounts: give it its IBANs on its card, or mark the movement as a transfer to it. A deposit is worth what went into it minus what came back.
new.title: New product
product.funds_hint: Each fund at today's value: its snapshot's, moved with its price.
product.funds_unknown: Its funds are unknown: record them on its card, in Settings › Accounts and products.
product.ibans_hint: A movement from another account of yours to one of these IBANs is a transfer to this product.
product.is_source: It is this account of your sources
product.name: Name
product.no_funds: It does not know its funds yet. Record them, or upload its portfolio in Hub.
product.rules_hint: They are removed in Settings › Rules.
product.shared_hint: What is paid from it goes to Shared.
product.tap_fund: Tap a fund to say what it is. Each one's value moves with its price since the snapshot.
product.title: Product
product.typed: You recorded this snapshot: it wins over its source's of the same day.
rules.hint: What you label by hand wins over any rule. A rule is created with “apply to the whole merchant” on a movement.
rules.in_order: In order: the first that matches decides
rules.keep_hint: The {movements} it explains stay labelled this way. Off, they are interpreted again without it.
rules.remove_hint: It stops applying to what arrives from now on.
rules.removed_kept: Rule removed · {movements} stay as they were
rules.title: Rules
settings.accounts_hint: Tap one to see where its data comes from, how it is valued and which funds it holds, and change what you want.
settings.categories_hint: What is not basic leaves basic spending (and the fund's target); what is not living, both.
settings.off_hint: “Does not match” compares the bank's balance with its movements of the last two months.
settings.unmapped: {count} accounts of your banks not assigned
settings.unmapped_body: {accounts}. Their movements are not shown until they are a product: create one, or assign it to one, in Accounts and products.
shared.cat_average: The shared money of each category, on average a month
shared.cat_year: The shared money of each category in {year}
shared.chart: The shared money of each month of {year}, by who paid, with what was yours
shared.closed: Each category across the {count} closed months of the year. The current month is left out.
shared.closes: {year}, not settled · settled when the year closes
shared.delete_consequence: It stops counting in the shared money of {year}.
shared.incomes_hint: They decide which part of the proportional belongs to each: each person's yearly net, by date ranges.
shared.kept_at: {other} keeps it in their Money · up to date {when}. What you record goes into the balance within half a minute.
shared.member_hint: {other} keeps the categories and settles each year in their Money. Your income and the space you see the shared money with are chosen in “Your income”.
shared.no_closed: No month of the year has ended: the average comes when the first one closes.
shared.no_keeper: Nobody keeps the shared account yet
shared.no_keeper_body: The shared money comes from the Money of whoever has the shared account. When they pick this space in their Shared, here you will see what they see, from your side.
shared.none_typed_body: What {other} pays out of pocket, or what you pay in cash with no withdrawal that explains it.
shared.ratio: How the proportional is split, by income
shared.ratio_hint: What is split in half counts half for each; the rest follows the declared income of the year. Yours is {percent}.
shared.reopen_detail: The year's balance counts as pending again.
shared.settle_detail: Say that you have already evened out this year. The balance is still shown, marked as settled.
shared.space_body: If the other person has the shared account in their Money, pick the space you share and here you will see what they see, from your side.
shared.space_question: Do you keep the shared money in an arga space?
shared.title: Shared
sheet.auto_detail: What you said about this movement is removed and Money decides it again.
sheet.auto_failed: Could not go back to automatic.
sheet.before_cutoff: It is from before the cut-off: that month is counted by the history, not by this.
sheet.fixed_detail: It stays fixed: no rule or sync changes it. You can go back to automatic whenever you want.
sheet.merchant_detail: A rule is created for this merchant. What you labelled by hand does not change.
sheet.return_hint: Interest or yield of the account. It does not count as income.
sheet.same_merchant: The same for this whole merchant?
sheet.same_merchant_body: There are {count} more movements from {merchant}. I can put “{name}” on all of them, also on those that arrive. What you labelled by hand does not change.
sheet.settlement_hint: A payment between you two to settle a part (paying back their half of something). It does not count as spending.
sheet.transfer_hint: Money between your accounts: neither expense nor income. If that account does not have this movement, Money records it there; when its statement arrives, the real one stays.
spending.before_hint: “Before” is {against} ({from} – {to}). The monthly average, of the last {months} closed months with spending.
spending.chart: Spending of each month, by category
spending.gaps_now: In {missing} of the {months} months of this period there is no individual spending recorded.
spending.gaps_previous: In {missing} of the {months} months of the previous period there is no individual spending recorded: the comparison comes out in your favour.
spending.history: {amount} come from history months, which keep the month's sum and not its movements.
spending.info_average: The spending of the period's closed months divided by them. The current month is left out: it carries only part of the spending and would lower the average.
spending.info_basic: What is not leisure, travel or work: what you need to live.
spending.info_other: What is not basic (leisure, travel) and what is not living expense (work).
spending.info_total: What you spent in the period: yours and, of the shared, your part (half, or your income ratio of the year), unless you choose “All”. A refund subtracts from its category. Below, against the previous period; if the period has not ended, against the same days of the previous one.
spending.lead_growing: {name} is what strays most from its average: {percent}
spending.lead_top: What you spend most on is {name}
spending.more: And {count} more: the rest, in Movements.
spending.title: Spending
spending.treemap: What was spent in the period, in blocks the size of each category
spending.widened: The 12 months up to the end of the period.
summary.aside: The cushion and where it is
summary.bars: Spending of each month, basic and the rest, with your average
summary.carried_sub: Worth that day's value, not today's
summary.history_hint: The months before {day} come from the history; since then, from your banks.
summary.info_basic: The same as monthly spending, but without what is not basic (Travel, Leisure): what you need to live. It is the base of the emergency fund target.
summary.info_cash: Money at hand: current and savings accounts, without the emergency fund. Shared accounts count whole, not by your share.
summary.info_emergency: The balance of the account that is your emergency fund, against its target: your basic monthly spending times the months you set in Settings.
summary.info_expense: What you spend a month, on average over the last 12 closed months: yours and your part of the shared, without what is not living expense (Work). With less than 12 months of data, the average is of those there are. Below, against the previous 12 months.
summary.info_liquid: Net worth without what you cannot take out at will, like the pension plan. Below, how much it changed in 12 months.
summary.info_month: What came in this month and where it went: your spending and your part of the shared, what you invested and what is left. It is Analysis' Flow for the current month.
summary.info_networth: What everything of yours is worth except real estate: accounts, funds, pension plan and crypto. Each account counts by your share (the shared one, half). Below, how much it changed in 12 months.
summary.no_data_body: When Money has accounts and movements, here you will see your net worth, your spending and your cushion.
summary.title: Summary
summary.trend: {label} at the end of each month, the last 12 months
tab.label: Sections
value.hint: From that day, the product starts from this value. If its source gives another on the same day, the source's wins.
value.title: What {name} is worth
why.ask: It is cash: tell me what it went on. You can split it across several categories.
why.auto: A rule decided it, or its bank's classification.
why.default: It carries its account's default category. If that is not it, change it.
why.manual: You labelled it. No rule changes it.
why.pending: No rule explains it. Tell me what it is.
why.return: Return of its account: neither expense nor income.
why.settlement: A payment between you two that settles a part: neither expense nor income.
why.transfer: Money between your accounts: neither expense nor income.
worth.carried: · Worth their last valuation plus what was contributed after:
worth.chart: Net worth at the end of each month, by type, with what was contributed
worth.down: Your net worth goes down {amount} a month on average
worth.estimated: · Estimated with their funds' prices since their last snapshot:
worth.estimated_end: They are corrected when another is uploaded.
worth.info_contributed: The money you have put in: cash accounts whole, and from each product what you contributed minus what you took out, not what it is worth.
worth.info_growth: What it is worth minus what was contributed: what the products have given you. If negative, they are worth less than you put in.
worth.info_total: What your accounts are worth on the last day of the period (or today, if it has not ended). A shared account counts by your share, unless you choose “All”. Below, against the day before the period starts.
worth.of_every_100: Of every 100 you have, {mine} you put in yourself
worth.title: Net worth
worth.up: Your net worth goes up {amount} a month on average
worth.widened: The 12 months up to the end of the period: one month alone draws no evolution.
